title: Progressive cordon-and-warmup with throughput corridor
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a maintenance workflow that cordons hosts progressively and warms replacement capacity before traffic is shifted, while guaranteeing a configured throughput corridor (min/max throughput) for each customer during maintenance windows.

Problem: Current rolling host upgrades cause short SLO regressions and token-cost spikes due to cold KV caches and non-deterministic drain timing. Dedicated customers require predictable throughput guarantees during scheduled maintenance so downstream SLAs don't violate.

Proposed solution summary:
- Introduce a 'cordon-and-warmup' stage that marks a host candidate for maintenance without draining immediately. We then allocate ephemeral warm hosts and pre-populate KV/prefix caches and model weights on the new hosts.
- Implement a throughput corridor controller that enforces a customer-level minimum throughput reservation and a ceiling during maintenance by borrowing from burst lanes or temporarily throttling non-critical routes.
- Autoscaler policy updates: add a hedging window that pre-provisions 10-30% extra capacity before maintenance and allows staged scaling down after warmup completes.
- Make upgrades declarative: maintenance job declares affected pools, desired warmup duration, corridor limits, and fallback model variant mapping. The controller executes checkpointed steps with rollbacks.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A scheduled maintenance job for a 200-host dedicated pool completes without customer P99 latency increasing >10% and sustained throughput drop <5% compared to baseline.
2) KV cache hit rate on replacement hosts reaches >= 70% within configured warmup window in integration tests.
3) Controller supports per-customer corridor configuration and logs corridor throttle decisions to Console.
4) Automated rollback triggers on >15% throughput degradation or >5% error rate increase.

Non-goals: ad-hoc emergency evacuations (we keep existing fast-evacuate path), full rewrite of autoscaler algorithms (only add hedging window and policy knobs).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-provisioning spikes cost. Mitigation: corridor controller can borrow from burst lanes with cost-tagging and post-mortem cost reports; default hedging percent is conservative (10%).
- Risk: Warmup may be ineffective for cold-start models. Mitigation: support model-variant fallbacks with quantized variants and preloaded weights; expose per-model warmup probes.

Implementation milestones:
1) Design spec and Console knobs (this ticket) -> 1 week.
2) Controller prototype: cordon state, warmup allocation, and simple corridor enforcement -> 2 sprint weeks.
3) Integration: KV prewarm hooks, autoscaler hedging policy, and PR to runtime for prefetch API -> 2 sprint weeks.
4) Canary run on a low-impact customer pool and metric validation -> 1 week.

Instrumentation: metric set to add: maintenance.cordon_duration, maintenance.warmup_kv_hit_rate, corridor.throttle_seconds, corridor.min_throughput_reserved, corridor.borrowed_capacity_cost_tags. All emitted as tags by customer and pool. Console dashboard PR required in release notes.
comments: 2026-01-25 | Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after on-call incident where a rolling upgrade caused a 22% throughput dip for a mid-market customer. Ticket scoped to avoid emergency evacuations and to focus on scheduled maintenance windows.

2026-01-28 | Diego Alvarez: Design review notes - propose a 10% default hedging capacity and make warmup duration configurable per model. Need to confirm runtime prefetch API surface with infra team. Added dependency on ENG-100512 for prewarm orchestration primitives.

2026-01-30 | Sarah Kim (Product): Product OKRs require per-customer corridor config exposed in Console. Suggest adding a 'maintenance policy' page and API to let customers opt into aggressive hedging at extra cost.

2026-02-02 | Diego Alvarez: Spike completed for cordon state machine and warmup allocator. Prototype: cordon -> allocate warm hosts -> run kv-prefill job -> health-checks -> gradual traffic cutover. Early local testing shows KV hit rate reaching ~58% in 90s for small models.

2026-02-03 | Aisha Patel: Added acceptance criteria and metrics. Please link PRs and Confluence design doc to this ticket before coding starts. Assigning to Diego for ownership of implementation and to Sofia (runtime) for prefetch API spec review.
notes: This approach aims to reduce SLO regression surface by decoupling drain timing from replacement readiness and by exposing explicit throughput contracts that the Console can surface to customers.
